Despite these advances, the BenLLM-Eval benchmark (Kabir et al., 2024) and subsequent evaluations (Bhowmik et al., 2025) consistently show that general-purpose large language models—including those marketed as multilingual—perform substantially worse on Bengali downstream tasks than on equivalent English tasks.

A 2025 evaluation of ten open-source LLMs across Bengali and English benchmarks likewise showed that Bengali performance was lower across model families, particularly for smaller models like Mistral, and that the gaps correlated with tokenization efficiency and model scale in ways consistent with data-volume explanations (Bhowmik et al., 2025).
cells.note: The paper presents an analytic synthesis of published benchmark evaluations rather than a new benchmark study. No numerical effect size is printed in the study text.

D.treatment: metaverse-based assessment with LLM virtual patients

O.outcome_detail: range and realism of clinical presentation and patient-doctor interaction

cells.quote: The developed platform allowed examinees to engage in dynamic history taking with AI-driven virtual patients and to perform basic virtual physical examinations within immersive three-dimensional environments. Scenarios such as abdominal pain accompanied by jaundice and ascites—difficult to replicate using human SPs—were effectively simulated. This flexibility substantially expands the range of assessable conditions, particularly for rare, complex, or logistically challenging cases in conventional OSCEs.
cells.note: Conceptual and prototype evidence from expert consensus and iterative review; no learner or examinee outcome comparison was conducted.

D.treatment: metaverse-based assessment with automated performance logging
D.comparison: conventional OSCE with standardized patient behavior and examiner judgment

O.outcome_detail: standardization, reproducibility, and objectivity of assessment data capture

cells.quote: A key advantage of the platform is its enhanced standardization. Unlike traditional OSCEs, which can be affected by variability in SP behavior and examiner judgment [9,10,21], virtual scenarios can be delivered consistently, reducing measurement error and supporting fairness. Furthermore, automated capture of examinee interactions enables objective evaluation and provides detailed assessment analytics for personalized formative feedback, which is often limited in conventional examinations [22,23].
cells.note: The article explicitly states that this was not evidence of psychometric superiority or educational effectiveness; claims are implementation-level and conceptual.

D.comparison: conventional physical examination or standardized-patient OSCE

O.outcome_detail: fidelity of tactile physical-examination performance

cells.quote: In addition, important limitations related to physical examination fidelity should be acknowledged. A metaverse-based platform can complement conventional OSCE stations that rely on written “result sheets” for findings that cannot be portrayed, by providing visual representations of clinical signs (e.g., jaundice and ascites) and a standardized, interactive workflow consistent with real clinical encounters. However, it cannot replace assessment components that require tactile or haptic feedback (e.g., palpation or percussion), limiting its suitability for certain physical examination competencies.
cells.note: This is a technical limitation identified through prototype development and expert evaluation, not a controlled comparison of learner performance.

O.outcome_detail: expert-detected hallucinations and contradictions

cells.quote: During the review of the 12 cases with MCQs, two cases of hallucinations were found, which are often overlooked problems. D.treatment: final tuned tutor with supervisor architecture

O.outcome_detail: hint-ceiling compliance under adversarial pressure

result.effect: 100% final compliance versus 54% initial; real compliance was about 77% after correcting an auditing artifact

cells.quote:
Starting point.The first billed run failed both pedagogy gates badly: a 43% earnest revise rate (G2) and 54% hint-ceiling compliance (G3), seemingly a system that both over-blocked honest students and leaked under pressure, a contradiction worth resolving first.

Rung 0, a measurement artifact.Sorting G3 rejections by cause (§4.4) showed that half of the apparent ceiling violations were grounding rejections, not over-help. The fault was in the auditor: it re-judged turns without the retrieved sources the live judge had seen, so it read every legitimate citation as unsupported. We proved this offline, at no further cost, then fixed it by persisting the sources the live judge saw and re-judging against them. Real ceiling compliance was about 77%, still failing, but now genuine.

End state.The final run passed both pedagogy gates: a 0% earnest revise rate (G2) and 100% hint-ceiling compliance, with zero rung breaches under adversarial pressure (G3), at a driven cost well under a dollar.
cells.note: Automated live test loop with scripted student personas, re-judged by a stronger auditing model; no human participants. The comparison is sequential rather than randomized, and the initial 54% included an identified measurement artifact.

cells.quote: One major limitation of the system is that it did not consistently preserve distractor logic.
cells.note: The study evaluated whether generated questions preserved the source questions' distractor logic, but it did not report a comparative learner outcome or a benchmark condition that supports a better/worse direction.

O.outcome_detail: Agreement on four-level gameplay-event classification

result.effect: quadratic-weighted Cohen's κ=0.841–0.855 versus experts; expert-expert κ=0.899–0.930

cells.quote: The LLM classifier achievesκ= 0.841–0.855against each expert—slightly below expert–expert pairs, but firmly in thealmost perfectrange according to the Landis–Koch scale.
cells.note: The study reports agreement rather than a manipulated learning intervention; direction is coded as lower agreement than expert–expert comparisons.

O.outcome_detail: Multi-rater agreement on gameplay-event classification

cells.quote: At the multi-rater level, Fleiss’κdrops only from 0.682 (three experts) to 0.624 (three experts + LLM), a reduction of 0.058 that preserves thesubstantialagreement tier.
cells.note: Adding the LLM slightly reduced multi-rater agreement.

O.outcome_detail: Correlation with learning gain

cells.quote: The single-LLM BKT baseline yields a small positive trend with learning gain (r= 0.095,p= 0.19) and post-test (r= 0.112,p= 0.12), but neither reaches statistical significance. In contrast, the Agentic BKT pipeline achieves a significant correlation with learning gain (r= 0.276,p= 0.0001) and post-test (r= 0.333,p <0.0001), approximately tripling the effect size relative to the baseline.
cells.note: The comparison is predictive validity against learning gain, not a randomized learning-outcome comparison.

O.outcome_detail: Correlation with post-test score

cells.quote: The single-LLM BKT baseline yields a small positive trend with learning gain (r= 0.095,p= 0.19) and post-test (r= 0.112,p= 0.12), but neither reaches statistical significance. In contrast, the Agentic BKT pipeline achieves a significant correlation with learning gain (r= 0.276,p= 0.0001) and post-test (r= 0.333,p <0.0001), approximately tripling the effect size relative to the baseline.

D.treatment: LLM-generated context-rich problems with thematic focuses

O.outcome_detail: Narrative and story-like quality of generated context-rich problems

cells.quote: The results were not satisfactory. The generated problems failed to mimic the story-like style of the original context-rich problems.
cells.note: Preliminary function test; the article reports no quantitative evaluation.

O.outcome_detail: evaluation leakage, measured as praise in agent replies

cells.quote:
The first attempt to suppress praise was a list of phrases the agent must never use. Praise increased.

The list was replaced by one principle, that the message after a correct answer must be indistinguishable from the message after a wrong one, together with a small set of permitted openers. In a bait test designed to draw praise (8 sessions, 16 agent replies), no reply contained it.
cells.note: The study reports scripted simulation evidence, not a randomized human comparison.

D.treatment: probing correct answers with a changed case

O.outcome_detail: detecting whether a correct idea holds under a changed case

cells.quote:
A single right-or-wrong item scores a student who caves and a student who holds identically, because both gave the correct first answer; only an instrument that probes correct answers can separate them.

Cave detection is proposed as an indicator of how robust a student’s understanding is, not only whether it is correct, and it is the core of the instrument.
cells.note: This is a proposed measurement rationale; no real students used the agent and no learning outcome was tested.

D.treatment: changed case altering exactly one variable

O.outcome_detail: tracing an answer change to a single idea

cells.quote: Each changed case had to alter exactly one variable; otherwise a changed answer could not be traced to a single idea.
cells.note: This is a design observation from adversarial simulations, not a validated human assessment result.

D.treatment: LLM system regenerated MCQs grouped around a shared scenario

O.outcome_detail: preservation of shared-scenario question structure

cells.quote: In this preliminary test, the generated questions preserved the same structure.
cells.note: The study describes this as a preliminary test in its work-in-progress section and provides no rubric evaluation or learner outcome data.

O.outcome_detail: LLM-judged faithfulness of generated responses

cells.quote: GPT-4o-mini and Claude 3 Haiku produced identical scores of 0 .77, whereas Gemini 2.5 Flash produced a lower score of 0.31. The variation across judges indicates that automated faithfulness evaluation is sensitive to the evaluator model.
cells.note: This is a secondary comparison of evaluator-model scores, not a randomized instructional treatment comparison or a reported learner learning outcome.
